Here are ten years of a monthly metric. It ended right about where it started. But ten years always hold a steep stretch. These four months rose twenty-five percent. Show just those months, and every number is real... and the story is false.

The Texas sharpshooter does it on purpose. Fire at a barn wall... then paint a target around the tightest cluster. Now fire again, and the cluster is gone. It was never aimed at. A pattern you found by looking has to hold up on fresh data.

Selection can manufacture a relationship, too. In this population, ability and interview score are unrelated. Now admit anyone whose two scores add up past a bar. Among the hundred and seven who get in, the correlation is minus zero point five six. Nothing changed anyone. A weak interview just means you got in on ability. So when you hear among our customers, ask what got them in.

And a correlation depends on what you're counting. Across six districts, average income and turnout correlate at zero point nine three. But inside a district, person by person, the correlation averages zero point zero seven. Both are true. One is about districts, the other about people. Name the unit before you quote a correlation.

Most of these traps share one flaw. The analysis was shaped by the data, instead of decided in advance. The cure is the same each time... decide what you'll test, before you look.
